title: Stars in the tail of the Antennae
caption: Part of the southern tidal tail of the Antennae Galaxies, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Antennae Galaxies, NGC 4038, NGC 4039 · constellation Corvus · about 45 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA & Ivo Saviane (European Southern Observatory)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Young blue stars crowd this view, strung along a stream of gas, while many red background galaxies peek through from far beyond. At higher zoom, thousands of faint red stars also fill the field. This is a stretch of the southern tail thrown out by the Antennae Galaxies, NGC 4038 and NGC 4039, a pair of galaxies in the middle of merging.

The blue stars formed only recently, out of gas that has piled up along the backbone of the tail. The two galaxies began interacting a few hundred million years ago, and scientists treat them as the textbook example of a galaxy merger, a benchmark for testing ideas about how galaxies change over time.

The faint red stars matter for another reason. Red giant stars cannot shine brighter than a certain limit, so their measured brightness works as a distance marker. Using them, astronomers concluded the Antennae sit closer than once believed.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.27 x 3.20 arcminutes) and distance (45 million light years), the frame spans roughly 43,000 × 42,000 light-years. Its light set out about 45 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This view comes from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys, using filters in visible light and the near-infrared. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The near-infrared part of the data is invisible to the eye, and the thousands of faint red stars are far too dim to see without a large telescope.

explore: The new measurement put the pair about 45 million light-years away, compared with the earlier best estimate of 65 million light-years. The Antennae rank among the nearest merging galaxies known, which is part of why they are studied so closely.
alt: A dark field scattered with young blue stars along a band of gas, with many small red background galaxies and faint red stars.
